result.summary: The street is a narrow residential corridor with continuous sidewalks on both sides but lacks dedicated pedestrian safety infrastructure such as marked crossings or traffic calming. Parked vehicles on both sides create visual obstructions for pedestrians, and a utility pole on the left sidewalk restricts the clear walking path.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A utility pole is located directly within the walking path on the left sidewalk, narrowing the effective width.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the narrow street creates significant sightline obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at potential crossing points to increase pedestrian visibility and shorten the crossing distance across the street.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility paint to clearly define pedestrian priority areas.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip or furniture zone to provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and the parking/travel lanes.

result.summary: This narrow residential street is characterized by row houses and a lack of pedestrian-friendly infrastructure beyond basic sidewalks. Safety is hindered by large parked vehicles that create significant blind spots and trash that obstructs the narrow walking paths.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Trucks
hazards.description: Large pickup trucks parked along the curb block the view of pedestrians for oncoming traffic and vice versa, especially near the alleyway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, parked along both sides of the street

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash cans and bags are placed directly on the narrow sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to navigate around them or step into the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side sidewalk in front of the white row house

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the alleyway and potential crossing points to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the alleyway or nearby intersections to reduce crossing distance and physically prevent parking in visibility zones.

interventions.title: Improved Trash Management
interventions.description: Implement better trash management and designated storage areas to keep the narrow sidewalks clear of debris for pedestrian passage.

result.summary: The street features narrow sidewalks directly adjacent to parallel parking lanes with no physical buffer or street trees. The roadway is wide and lacks lane markings, which may encourage higher vehicle speeds, and there are no marked pedestrian crossings visible in the immediate vicinity.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along both sides of the street block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the midblock section.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Crossings
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks are visible, forcing pedestrians to cross an unmarked, wide roadway.

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a relatively wide street can lead to higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable positioning.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image, the asphalt roadway.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at the upcoming intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing/Markings
interventions.description: Add lane markings to define travel lanes and parking lanes, which helps to naturally slow traffic.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is highly hostile, with no dedicated or protected walkway visible. Vehicles are parked directly against the building frontage, completely obstructing any potential pedestrian path and forcing people to walk in the roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles occupy the entire space between the building and the roadway, leaving no room for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and mid-ground along the building frontage

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Separation
hazards.description: There is no curb or physical barrier separating the roadway from the building edge, creating a high risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflict.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire street edge visible in the image

interventions.title: Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install a raised, ADA-compliant sidewalk with a minimum 6-foot clear width to provide a safe, dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Parking Management and Enforcement
interventions.description: Implement clear parking regulations and physical barriers like bollards to prevent vehicles from parking on the pedestrian walkway.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety during nighttime hours.
